usage.callShape: GET https://url-extractor.x402.paysponge.com/url/:domain where :domain is a bare hostname (e.g. vercel.com), no body
quirks: The :domain path segment is a bare hostname (e.g. 'vercel.com'), NOT a full URL with scheme/path.

It only reads the target site's /sitemap.xml. If the domain has no sitemap, you STILL get charged $0.01 and receive HTTP 422 {error:'No URLs found in sitemap', count:0} -- pick a domain you know publishes a sitemap.
example.com has no sitemap and returns 422; use a real content site to get a 200.
Response can be very large (vercel.com returned ~766KB / 6975 urls) -- expect big payloads for big sites.
usage.guide: Call GET https://url-extractor.x402.paysponge.com/url/<domain> with the bare hostname in the path (e.g. /url/vercel.com), no request body; pay the $0.01 x402 quote (USDC on Base). On success you get HTTP 200 with {sitemap, count, urls:[{url, lastmod}]} -- read the link list from body.urls. The service only parses the domain's /sitemap.xml, so if the site lacks one you are still charged and get a 422 with count:0; only point it at domains you know publish a sitemap. Large sites return very large responses (thousands of URLs).
